series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 5.2 · October 2026
title: CPAT-AI: Rebuilding a Policy Model

slides.title: CPAT-AI: Rebuilding a Policy Model as a Transparent, Testable Tool
slides.subtitle: What two AI-assisted rebuilds of the Climate Policy Assessment Tool found
slides.message: Rebuilt twice in October 2026 under one rule (fix bugs, copy and log deliberate choices), legacy CPAT turned out to hold 228 bugs, 24 of them serious. Building it a second time found seven bugs in the first rebuild.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: CPAT shapes reform advice, but no one could audit its legacy workbook

slides.text: Formulas differ from row to row, so checking one row says little about the next. Audits of large spreadsheets almost always find errors.
slides.source: CPAT Documentation (2023); CPAT-AI task log (2026); Panko (1998); Powell, Baker and Lawson (2008).

slides.title: One rule kept the rebuild faithful: fix bugs, copy deliberate choices, decide departures in writing

points.text: is a formula that does not compute what it means to (a wrong row, a term applied twice). Fixed, never copied.
is a deliberate choice open to question (an old data vintage). Copied exactly and logged for the modelers.
needs a dated decision by the model's named owner.

points.lead: So every difference from the original

slides.title: Two rebuilds and shared codes turn every comparison into a table join

slides.title: Building twice found seven bugs, but versions built from one reading can share an error

points.lead: Python found seven bugs in Excel-AI,
points.text: e.g. nominal GDP divided by a billion when already in billions; two gas price series swapped. All fixed in both.
27 independently written programs failed together far more than chance predicts (Knight and Leveson 1986).
48 agent-written versions showed the same, though voting across three cut failures by about two thirds (Ron et al. 2026).
test 1 ties every block to legacy's own results, which no agent wrote; fixes go to the CPAT team.

slides.source: CPAT-AI register (M15-M22); Knight and Leveson (1986); Ron, Baudry and Monperrus (2026).

slides.title: AI agents built the models; a named owner made every judgment

points.text: through Claude Code and GitHub Copilot: builders, checks, the Python model, the register's documents.
carries a dated owner decision; the owner accepted each release.

points.lead: The evidence on AI productivity is mixed:
points.text: 56% faster on a set task (Peng et al. 2023); 19% slower for experienced developers on mature projects (Becker et al. 2025).

points.lead: So the safeguard is the test, not the tool.
points.text: Every output was checked by something its author did not write.

slides.source: CPAT-AI task log, 2-29 October 2026; Peng et al. (2023); Becker et al. (2025).
